source.title: Closing the Activation-Cone Blind Spot: Response-Time Probing and Unified Defense

page_placements.theme: Geometry and low-rank proxies do not establish safety-specific mechanisms

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether compliant prefilling and adversarial suffixes bypass safety behavior, using attack-success rates across models and inference-time defenses rather than the original fine-tuning or token-KL measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the shallow-alignment and fine-tuning findings from Qi et al.; those are not this study's results. Probe AUROCs, benign FPRs, and steering-geometry measurements do not themselves measure harmful compliance; geometry results are recorded under fits_no_version. Results for other attacks such as AutoDAN and DeepInception are not included because they do not test the versions here.
record.test_reason: Reports no-defense attack success rates for compliant prefilling and GCG suffixes on newer instruction-tuned models (Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B). These numbers bear directly on V4, although the paper is mainly about defenses. The study's own defense results (response-halt, dual-probe, unified) and the prompt-time defense comparisons measure defense performance, not whether shallow safety exists.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also present the no-defense prefilling ASRs as confirming Qi et al.'s shallow-alignment finding, and call prefilling the hardest attack for prompt-time defenses (28–75% ASR). Their main conclusion is about defenses: single-layer activation-cone gates are structurally blind to prefilling, while response-time probing with halt blocks the canonical template family. They scope this to template- and probe-depth-dependent generalisation and uneven adaptive robustness.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates inference-time defenses against prefilling and suffix attacks; it does not perform the original harmful or benign fine-tuning interventions or the per-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Prefilling results vary by model and defense. Probe behavior varies with template, layer depth, judge window, and adaptive-attack form; the paper reports that cross-template generalization depends on probe depth and notes an unexplained Qwen-2.5 counterexample.

fits_no_version.finding: AlphaSteer's null-space projection norm moves in opposite directions under prefilling: it falls on 89.5% of Llama pairs and rises on 92.1% of Mistral pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prefilling-induced activation shifts at a fixed layer differ by model.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine to the benign-mean activation falls under prefilling on all pairs for both models, disagreeing with the projection measure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-direction benign references misrepresent prefilled-activation geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Static refusal-vector steering raises Llama prefilling ASR from 53% to 75%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal steering can amplify prefilling compliance rather than counter it.

record.problems: Most cross-paradigm attack evaluations use n=40; the paper notes cross-template generalization failures and uneven adaptive robustness. The claimed Mistral distribution-shift mechanism is inferred rather than directly verified. Steering is fixed at layer 14 without a relative-depth sweep. Probe weights for Mistral and Llama drift under current library versions, although fresh retraining recovers the reported results. Some results use a keyword heuristic; LLM-judge rescoring changes some ASRs.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row cap, omitted Table 1 GCG results for static steering, CAST, prompt-time probe-gated steering, and dual/unified methods where applicable. Also omitted the remaining n=200 attack-type comparisons, novel-template detection-rate analyses, and the individual adaptive rows not needed to show the reported variation. These appear in Tables 1, 5, 8–10 and Appendices R, S, and U.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning; the paper states fine-tuning robustness was not evaluated.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Decoding changes are not tested. No-defense prefilling ASR is reported only for 4 of 7 models in Table 1.
Not tested. A probe transfer from instruct to base models (AUROC ~0.70) is about detection, not about why safety is shallow.

missing.what: No-defense prefilling ASR at n=200: Mistral 71.5%, Llama 64.5%. No-defense GCG ASR at n=200: Mistral 71.5%, Llama 1.5%.

Gemma-4-31B shows very low harm under prefilling with a 30-token judge (63/645 training samples harmful, 0/50 test). Llama, Qwen3 and Gemma-4 show 0–2% harm on novel canonical-register prefill templates, and Llama refused all 40 without defense on some distributions. This means prefilling success depends on template and model.
missing.locator: App. R; App. Y; Table 12 footnote

missing.what: Per-template no-defense attack validity tiers for 20 held-out prefill templates (primary ≥50%, secondary 25–50%, excluded <25%).
Llama Guard 3 flags 0/40 prefilling responses even though 70–100% contain harmful content.

record.verdict_notes: Only the no-defense attack rows bear on V4. All defense cells, including the study's own probe methods, are relinked to none. ASR uses a keyword heuristic at n=40, and no no-attack baseline is given. The Gemma-2 and Qwen-2.5 rows are paper-environment results, while the Mistral and Llama rows are current-environment. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of refusal after fine-tuning.
No benign-data fine-tuning or measurement of harmful compliance after benign fine-tuning.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models.
Tests compliant prefilling and GCG suffix attacks, but not decoding changes or fine-tuning as bypasses. Adaptive and novel-template results are limited to the settings reported.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether data or training objectives produce safety shallowness.
No training intervention designed to deepen safety across response tokens.
